countryWithoutUnderstanding.title: Changing countries without understanding what the system rewards
countryWithoutUnderstanding.description: Immigrating thinking effort alone is enough, without analyzing the target country's real success mechanisms.
countryWithoutUnderstanding.context: Competent professional leaving a problem rent country for a stability-redistribution country, expecting to be rewarded for their added value alone.
countryWithoutUnderstanding.money: Investment in wrong certifications or networks

diplomasInNetworkSystem.money: Cost of studies without proportional return

stabilityInGrowthSystem.title: Seeking stability in a growth system
stabilityInGrowthSystem.description: Expecting strong social protections and predictable progression in a country that rewards risk and velocity.
stabilityInGrowthSystem.context: French professional emigrating to the US expecting a stable permanent contract with guaranteed health and retirement benefits.

growthInStabilitySystem.title: Seeking rapid growth in a stability system
growthInStabilitySystem.description: Trying to scale quickly or disrupt in a country that values prudence, processes, and protection of acquired rights.
growthInStabilitySystem.context: American tech entrepreneur launching a startup in France expecting the same velocity and flexibility as California.

visibilityInRentSystem.title: Succeeding visibly without protection in a rent system
visibilityInRentSystem.description: Publicly displaying financial or professional success without having built necessary protections.
visibilityInRentSystem.context: Prosperous entrepreneur in a problem rent country showing success on social media without political network or protection.

bettingAgainstState.title: Betting against state direction in a hybrid system
bettingAgainstState.description: Investing or engaging in sectors the state has decided to control or discourage.
bettingAgainstState.context: Foreign investor betting on a growing sector in China without understanding incoming political restriction signals.

expectingPermanenceExtraction.title: Expecting permanence in an extraction system
expectingPermanenceExtraction.description: Planning a permanent life in a resource country that only gives temporary contracts to foreigners.
expectingPermanenceExtraction.context: Expat in a Gulf country buying real estate and taking on debt hoping to stay permanently.
expectingPermanenceExtraction.energy: Permanent uncertainty about the long term
expectingPermanenceExtraction.money: Assets difficult to liquidate on departure
expectingPermanenceExtraction.stagnation: Neither belonging nor prepared plan B

ignoringLocalCredentials.context: Foreign doctor or lawyer in Switzerland or Germany refusing to retake local equivalencies.

origin.title: Why this tool exists
origin.paragraph1: This tool was created by someone who lost years making choices without understanding the system they were operating in.
origin.paragraph2: Wrong country, wrong career, wrong timing — not from lack of intelligence, but from lack of a framework.
origin.paragraph3: Pyramid Compass was born from this frustration: to give everyone the analysis that only the privileged receive from their network.
origin.conclusion: This is not a tool that tells you what to do. It's a tool that helps you SEE — so YOU decide with full knowledge.

forEveryone.title: For everyone
forEveryone.subtitle: Whatever your starting point, you deserve access to information.

q1.question: Can Pyramid Compass tell me which country to choose?
q1.answer: No. The tool analyzes systems and simulates scenarios, but the final decision is yours. We provide information, you make your own choices.

q2.question: Is the data reliable?
q2.answer: We use public sources (corruption indices, tax data, passport rankings). This data is indicative and may change. Always verify with official sources before making important decisions.

q3.question: What's the difference between "My simulation" and "Educational mode"?
q3.answer: "My simulation" (Exit Keys) analyzes YOUR real situation with YOUR parameters. "Educational mode" has you play a FICTIONAL random character to understand mechanics without personal involvement.

q4.question: Is it free?
q4.answer: Yes, the tool is free. You can create an account to sync your data across devices, but it's not required.

q5.question: Is my personal data protected?
q5.answer: Simulation data stays on your device or in your personal account. We don't sell your data and don't share it with anyone.

q6.question: Can I use this tool for important decisions?
q6.answer: This tool is a starting point for your reflection, not an absolute source of truth. For important decisions (immigration, taxes, health), always consult qualified professionals.

countries.title: Country Analysis
countries.subtitle: In-depth analysis of national systems. Understand what each system rewards, the risks, and your options.

cameroon.name: Cameroon
cameroon.ruleOfGold: Never solve a visible problem. Never become indispensable. Never centralize.

pyramid.realAsset: The problem itself — dysfunction is profitable

whoLoses: The young and ambitious without networks

plan30Days: Identify one exportable skill to develop
plan12Months: Create first offshore account if possible
playbook.planB: Focus on French-speaking destinations with easier visa access (Morocco, Senegal, France, Canada-Quebec). Build digital skills for remote work.

france.name: France
france.ruleOfGold: The system protects stability, not explosion. Play the long game within the rules.
whoWins: Those who master the system rules
Those with right diplomas and networks

playbook.planB: EU mobility is your advantage. Consider Portugal, Spain, or Netherlands for lower friction. Switzerland for higher ambition. Keep French benefits while building elsewhere.

switzerland.name: Switzerland
switzerland.ruleOfGold: Excellence + rules + reputation = security. No shortcuts, no approximations.

pyramid.base: Citizens invested in maintaining the system

playbook.planB: Other COMPETENCE_TRUST systems: Germany, Netherlands, Austria, Singapore. Build credentials that transfer across these systems.

usa.name: United States
usa.ruleOfGold: Win fast, secure gains, diversify. The system rewards velocity, not stability.
whoLoses: Those relying on social safety net

playbook.planB: Consider Canada for stability with growth, Portugal for EU access, Dubai for tax optimization. Keep US income while building options.

germany.name: Germany
germany.ruleOfGold: Precision, process, and patience. The system rewards those who master the rules.

pyramid.base: Taxpayers supporting the social market economy

playbook.planB: Similar systems: Austria, Switzerland, Netherlands. German qualifications are highly transferable in EU.

uae.name: United Arab Emirates
uae.ruleOfGold: Be useful to power, stay discreet, never go local. Your gains are yours as long as you follow the rules.

pyramid.top: Ruling families and their inner circles
pyramid.institutions: State structures serving the royal vision
pyramid.realAsset: Access to power and usefulness to the system

whoWins: Those who understand the red lines
whoLoses: Those who forget they are guests

do: Maintain low profile on sensitive topics
plan30Days: Open local and international bank accounts
Identify red lines not to cross
playbook.planB: Options to consider: Portugal or Spain for EU, Singapore for Asia, Mauritius for favorable taxation with residence.

nigeria.name: Nigeria
nigeria.ruleOfGold: Hustle or disappear. The system rewards agility, not conformity.

pyramid.institutions: Weak state with pockets of competence

dont: Depend on a single income source
playbook.planB: Ghana for regional stability, UK or Canada for established diaspora, Dubai for business. Develop tech skills for global mobility.

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.ruleOfGold: Excellence + conformity + added value = permission to stay. No room for mediocrity.

do: Respect all rules to the letter
playbook.planB: Hong Kong for finance, Malaysia MM2H for cost of living, Australia for citizenship. Build transferable Asia-Pacific skills.

portugal.name: Portugal
portugal.ruleOfGold: Patience and quality of life. The system offers EU access in exchange for time and capital.

pyramid.realAsset: EU access and quality of life

whoWins: Those with capital or passive income
Digital nomads with strong currency income

do: Take advantage of NHR tax regime if eligible
playbook.planB: Spain for more economic opportunities, Malta for taxation, France for French speakers. Portuguese passport opens all of EU.

morocco.name: Morocco
morocco.ruleOfGold: Respect the codes, build relationships, stay discreet about power.

pyramid.top: Monarchy and circles close to power

whoLoses: Those who openly challenge the system

playbook.planB: France for French-speaking diaspora, Spain for proximity, UAE for business. Morocco can be an Africa hub.

canada.name: Canada
canada.ruleOfGold: Immigrate by the rules, integrate patiently, build for the long term.
whoWins: Those who follow the process patiently
Those who integrate into local culture
whoLoses: Those who don't adapt to climate

playbook.planB: USA for opportunities (if visa possible), Australia for similar climate, UK for Commonwealth ties.

brazil.name: Brazil
brazil.ruleOfGold: Jeitinho and relationships. The formal system exists, but the real game is informal.

pyramid.realAsset: Network and ability to navigate the system

whoWins: Those with good network (QI = Quem Indica)
whoLoses: Those who don't adapt to culture

playbook.planB: Portugal for EU (common language), Argentina for region, USA for opportunities. Brazil can be a Latin America hub.

uk.name: United Kingdom
uk.ruleOfGold: Competence + network + perseverance. The system is open but competitive.

dont: Depend on healthcare system without backup
playbook.planB: Ireland for EU access + English-speaking, USA for opportunities, Canada for similar lifestyle. UK remains global financial hub.

japan.name: Japan
japan.ruleOfGold: Conformity, patience, and mastery. The system rewards those who truly integrate.

playbook.planB: Singapore for English-speaking Asia, South Korea for similar culture, Taiwan for more relaxed environment. Japan requires total commitment.

australia.name: Australia
australia.ruleOfGold: Skills + points = access. The system is meritocratic but selective.
whoWins: Those who pass the points system
Those who adapt to Australian lifestyle
whoLoses: Those without skills on the list

do: Target skills on the skills list
playbook.planB: New Zealand for easier access, Canada for similar system, Singapore for Asia-Pacific. Australia offers excellent quality of life.

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.ruleOfGold: Be direct, be competent, be integrated. The system rewards those who contribute.

playbook.planB: Netherlands offers EU hub with English. Consider Germany for more opportunities, Belgium for lower costs, or UK for pure English environment.

china.name: China
china.ruleOfGold: Align publicly with the Party, build privately. Never become a political symbol.

pyramid.institutions: State apparatus mixing control and market
pyramid.gatekeepers: Party connections, guanxi networks, regulatory approvals

whoWins: Those who read political winds correctly
whoLoses: Those growing too fast too visibly

do: Invest in skills that transfer globally
playbook.planB: Singapore, Japan, or Taiwan for similar cultures. Portugal, Canada for different environments. Keep skills exportable and assets diversified.

russia.name: Russia
russia.ruleOfGold: Never challenge power publicly. The state giveth and the state taketh away.

pyramid.realAsset: Loyalty to power and useful invisibility

whoWins: Those close to power without threatening it

dont: Build business dependent on single sector
playbook.planB: Georgia, Armenia, Serbia for easier entry. EU countries for longer-term. Keep passport valid, skills current, assets mobile.

brazil.name: Brazil
brazil.ruleOfGold: Navigate the jeitinho - flexibility, networks, and patience beat formal rules.

pyramid.top: Political class and major business families
pyramid.institutions: Complex bureaucracy mixing formal and informal
pyramid.base: Workers in formal and informal economies

dont: Expect things to work like home country
playbook.planB: Portugal for language/culture similarity. Other Latin American countries. US or EU with right visa. Keep options open.

norway.name: Norway
norway.ruleOfGold: The collective comes first. Excellence is good but never above the group.

plan30Days: Research job market in your field
playbook.planB: Other Nordic countries, Netherlands, Germany for similar stability. Lower cost options in Southern Europe with EU mobility.

qatar.name: Qatar
qatar.ruleOfGold: Be useful, stay quiet, plan your exit. You are a guest with an expiration date.

pyramid.top: Al Thani royal family and close circles
pyramid.institutions: State structures serving vision and stability
pyramid.realAsset: Usefulness to state projects and discretion

playbook.planB: UAE for similar region. Singapore for Asia. Portugal, Malta for EU access. Have multiple options ready.

venezuela.name: Venezuela
venezuela.ruleOfGold: Survive, stay invisible, prepare your exit. The system rewards only those at the very top.

playbook.planB: Colombia, Peru, Chile for proximity. Spain for cultural ties. US with right visa. Move as soon as possible.

saudi-arabia.name: Saudi Arabia
saudi-arabia.ruleOfGold: Serve the vision, respect the values, know your place. High rewards for the useful, high risks for the visible.

playbook.planB: UAE, Bahrain for regional options. Portugal, Malta for EU. Canada, Australia for permanent options. Plan carefully.

india.name: India
india.ruleOfGold: Navigate the paradox of ancient systems and explosive growth. Relationships and resilience beat pure credentials.

pyramid.institutions: Dense bureaucracy mixing colonial legacy and digital future
pyramid.valueCreators: Entrepreneurs in formal and informal sectors

playbook.planB: UAE, Singapore for nearby options. US, UK, Canada for developed markets. Keep skills exportable.

turkey.name: Turkey
turkey.ruleOfGold: Ride the volatility if you can, hedge if you must. Political winds change fast.

pyramid.top: Presidential circle and aligned business groups

do: Earn in hard currency if possible
playbook.planB: EU countries via citizenship programs. Georgia, Serbia for easy entry. UAE for regional option. Keep assets mobile.

lottery.label: The Shortcut Seeker
lottery.description: You want an immediate exit, a break from your current situation, a shortcut.
lottery.workRelation: Low engagement with long-term work — effort feels pointless if slow.
lottery.riskRelation: Often high but poorly controlled — unconscious risk-taking.
lottery.whatWorks: Strict budgeting if gambling, parallel Plan B with stable income and useful skills.
lottery.trap: Waiting for 'the sign', going into debt, believing opportunity replaces strategy.

comfort.label: Comfort & Zero Stress
comfort.description: You seek tranquility, routine, and psychological security.
comfort.workRelation: You want structure, clear expectations, defined framework.
comfort.whatWorks: Stability, slow but certain progression, automatic savings, predictable job.
comfort.trap: Getting bored, fading out, then exploding after a few years.

builder.label: Patient Builder
builder.description: You want wealth + pride + the feeling of having earned it.
builder.workRelation: Ready to work, but effort must make sense and actually pay off.
builder.whatWorks: Simple business, rare skills, discipline, long-term investing.
builder.trap: Going too complex too early, scattering, inventing sophisticated strategies before having the basics.

safeWealth.label: Safe Wealth Builder
safeWealth.description: You want high income with maximum security.
safeWealth.workRelation: OK with working, but not with putting yourself at risk.
safeWealth.whatWorks: Increase income via rare skills, secure via diversification, insurance, long-term strategy.
safeWealth.trap: Internal contradiction (wanting jackpot without trade-offs) → stagnation.

nomad.label: Global Nomad
nomad.description: You seek geographic freedom and autonomy.
nomad.workRelation: You want to work from anywhere.
nomad.whatWorks: Remote jobs, income in strong currency, understanding of visas, rules, and logistics.

purpose.label: Purpose-Driven
purpose.riskRelation: Often moderate, but emotion can push you to forget yourself.
purpose.whatWorks: Useful jobs + clear limits + anti-burnout system + self-care + protection framework.
purpose.trap: Sacrificing yourself, burning out, confusing value with suffering.

status.label: Status Seeker
status.description: You seek recognition, respect, social identity.
status.riskRelation: Moderate to high depending on ego and competition.
status.whatWorks: Excellence, selectivity, network, storytelling, career strategy.
status.trap: Toxic comparison, performance anxiety, fragile identity if status drops.

recovery.label: Recovery & Rebuilding
recovery.description: You seek security, control, repair, emotional stability, reconstruction.
recovery.workRelation: Need for mastery, sometimes fear of instability.
recovery.riskRelation: Low at first, then increases as security returns.
recovery.whatWorks: Stabilize first (income, framework, routine), then progressive ramp-up, clear plan, realistic goals.
recovery.trap: Judging yourself, trying to catch up 10 years in 6 months, exhausting yourself.

concept.title: The Concept
concept.description: PYRAMIDS is a strategy game where you manage life trajectories. You don't choose your starting point: you draw characters with a birth country, traits, and aspirations. Each 'year' of play, you make decisions: work, study, heal, migrate, start a business, build your network, nurture relationships... The world moves, countries have their rules, and success depends on your ability to optimize under constraints.
concept.quote: You win by managing your life better than others, with a system that stays realistic.

pyramidsLife.title: The 6 Life Pyramids
pyramidsLife.description: The board represents 6 life domains, scaling from 0 to 5. Climbing a pyramid makes your life more 'successful' in that domain, but almost always at a cost elsewhere.

welcome.title: Welcome to the Game of Life
welcome.content: This game simulates the realities that millions of people experience around the world. This is not fiction — it's a mirror of the real world, with its opportunities and dangers.
welcome.reality: Every mechanic in this game reflects a lived reality. Our goal is prevention and understanding, not fear.

lifeAssignment.title: You don't choose your starting life
lifeAssignment.content: Like in real life, you don't choose where you're born, your starting economic situation, or your initial constraints. The game assigns you a random life — some easier, some very difficult.
lifeAssignment.reality: Being born in a stable country with a good passport is a privilege. Others must fight for rights that many take for granted.
examples: A Swiss born in Geneva vs a Nigerian born in Lagos — same ambitions, very different opportunities
A woman born in Saudi Arabia vs one born in Canada — fundamentally different freedoms
A child born into a wealthy family vs a poor one — same country, different trajectories

resources.title: Your life resources
resources.content: You manage 6 essential resources: Health, Money, Network, Security, Education and Morale. Every decision affects them. If some drop to zero, consequences can be severe.
resources.reality: In real life, losing your health or network can mean the end of all opportunities. Money alone doesn't protect from everything.
examples: Health: a chronic illness changes the entire expatriation calculation
Network: without contacts, even skills aren't enough
Security: a weak passport drastically limits options

pyramids.title: Every country has its system
pyramids.content: The 6 pyramid types represent how each country actually works. Some reward competence, others connections, others resource extraction.
pyramids.reality: Understanding a country's system is crucial. What works in Germany can be fatal in Cameroon, and vice versa.

events.title: Life sends you events
events.content: Each turn, global and local events affect your resources. Economic crises, opportunities, natural disasters, political changes — you must adapt.
events.reality: Nobody controls everything. Migrants who planned everything can see their plans destroyed by a policy change overnight.
examples: A global economic crisis can wipe out years of savings
A new government can close borders or change visa rules

actions.title: Your choices define your trajectory
actions.content: Each turn, you can work, study, network, save, or take risks. Major actions have more impact but carry more risk.
actions.reality: Every choice has an opportunity cost. Studying means less immediate money. Working hard without a network may lead nowhere.

shortcuts.title: Dangerous shortcuts
shortcuts.content: The game offers 'shortcuts' — illegal crossing, undocumented work, fake documents. These options exist because they exist in real life. Consequences can be catastrophic.
shortcuts.reality: Every year, thousands of people die attempting these shortcuts. In Libya, human trafficking is a reality. This game doesn't glorify these choices — it shows their real consequences.
examples: Mediterranean crossing: real risk of death, interception, or slavery
Fake documents: imprisonment, deportation, permanent ban
Undocumented work: exploitation, no protection, total vulnerability

aspirations.title: Your personal goals
aspirations.content: Your character has aspirations — becoming wealthy, living safely, reuniting with family, or simply surviving. Success is measured against YOUR goals, not a universal standard.
aspirations.reality: 'Success' is relative. A refugee who rebuilds their life has accomplished as much as an entrepreneur who becomes a millionaire.

endgame.title: Life summary
endgame.content: At the end, the game evaluates whether you achieved your aspirations, preserved your health, and navigated the system. There's no 'right' way to play — only choices and their consequences.
endgame.reality: This game is a tool for understanding. Whether it helps you appreciate your situation or better understand others', that's its real victory.

keyConcept.title: Key concept: Trend ≠ Certainty
keyConcept.explanation: When the tool says 'this system tends to favor X', it means statistically, in this type of context, X is more likely. But YOUR particular case depends on thousands of factors the tool doesn't know.
keyConcept.analogy: It's like weather: 'It often rains in November in Paris' is statistically true, but it doesn't predict whether it will rain on November 15th when YOU are there.

universalErrors.title: Universal Errors Library
universalErrors.subtitle: The 10 most costly decision errors. No moralizing, just facts and tools to avoid them.
universalErrors.intro: These errors are not moral failings. They are recurring patterns that cost time, money, and energy. Recognizing them allows you to anticipate them.
universalErrors.simulateDescription: Test a decision related to this error to identify risks before committing.
universalErrors.ctaTitle: Do you recognize one of these errors?
universalErrors.ctaDescription: Run your decision through the prevention filter to identify risks before it's too late.

systemError.name: System Error
systemError.shortDescription: Ignoring the real rules of the system you operate in.
systemError.definition: Acting according to personal expectations rather than the actual rules of the system (tax, legal, social) you're subject to.
systemError.whyItHappens: We often project rules from our home country or familiar environment onto a new context. Reliable information is hard to find and systems are complex.
systemError.timeCost: 6 months to 2 years of procedures or adaptation

metricError.name: Metric Error
metricError.shortDescription: Optimizing the wrong indicator or measuring only what reassures.
metricError.definition: Focusing on superficial indicators (gross salary, prestige) while ignoring metrics that truly matter (quality of life, real cost, progress).
metricError.whyItHappens: Visible metrics are easy to communicate and compare. Important metrics are often invisible or uncomfortable to measure.
metricError.timeCost: Years spent chasing the wrong goal
metricError.moneyCost: Investments in areas that bring nothing

timingError.name: Timing Error
timingError.shortDescription: Acting too early, too late, or ignoring system cycles.
timingError.definition: Not accounting for economic, seasonal, or institutional cycles that determine an action's success.
timingError.whyItHappens: Impatience pushes for immediate action. Long cycles are hard to perceive when you're in them.
timingError.energyCost: Frustration of swimming against the current

irreversibilityError.name: Irreversibility Error
irreversibilityError.shortDescription: Committing to a hard-to-correct decision without testing it.
irreversibilityError.definition: Making a high-commitment decision (marriage, property purchase, permanent expatriation) without a test phase or possible withdrawal.
irreversibilityError.whyItHappens: Social pressure values total commitment. Testing before committing is sometimes seen as lack of confidence.
irreversibilityError.timeCost: Years correcting a mistake or living with it
irreversibilityError.moneyCost: Very high exit costs (divorce, selling at a loss)

hiddenCostError.name: Hidden Cost Error
hiddenCostError.shortDescription: Underestimating real costs beyond the displayed price.
hiddenCostError.definition: Only seeing visible costs (price, salary) while ignoring hidden costs (maintenance, stress, time, lost opportunities).
hiddenCostError.whyItHappens: Sellers and systems minimize hidden costs. Our brain prefers simple numbers to complex calculations.
hiddenCostError.timeCost: Invisible hours of maintenance and management

egoError.name: Ego Error
egoError.shortDescription: Letting status or image guide economic decisions.
egoError.definition: Making decisions based on what you want to project rather than what you actually need.
egoError.whyItHappens: Social status is a fundamental human need. Others' perceptions influence our choices more than we admit.
egoError.moneyCost: Status purchases at the expense of security
egoError.energyCost: Anxiety related to keeping up appearances

environmentError.name: Environment Error
environmentError.shortDescription: Ignoring the environment's influence on your results.
environmentError.definition: Believing success depends only on personal effort while ignoring the role of context (country, network, era, sector).
environmentError.whyItHappens: Meritocracy is a dominant narrative. Acknowledging the environment's role can seem to diminish one's merits.
environmentError.timeCost: Years stagnating in the wrong environment
environmentError.moneyCost: Unrealized potential due to poor positioning

narrativeError.name: Narrative Error
narrativeError.shortDescription: Confusing an inspiring story with an applicable strategy.
narrativeError.definition: Following a narrative (success story, guru advice) without verifying if it applies to your own situation.
narrativeError.whyItHappens: Stories are more memorable than statistics. Survivorship bias makes successes more visible than failures.
narrativeError.moneyCost: Investments in irrelevant training or advice
narrativeError.energyCost: Self-doubt when promised results don't arrive

sunkCost.name: Sunk Cost
sunkCost.shortDescription: Continuing to invest because you've already invested too much.
sunkCost.definition: Pursuing an unfavorable action because you've already committed time, money, or energy you don't want to lose.
sunkCost.whyItHappens: Our brain hates losses. Admitting a past mistake is painful. We hope the situation will improve.
sunkCost.timeCost: Additional years in a dead end
sunkCost.moneyCost: Additional investments to justify previous ones
sunkCost.energyCost: Exhaustion maintaining something that doesn't work

socialProofError.name: Social Proof Error
socialProofError.shortDescription: Imitating others without checking if their situation applies to yours.
socialProofError.definition: Following the majority's or admired figures' behavior without analyzing if their constraints and goals are the same.
socialProofError.whyItHappens: Following the group reduces uncertainty. If others do it this way, it must be the right method.
socialProofError.timeCost: Years following a path that isn't yours
socialProofError.energyCost: Gap between aspirations and daily life
